{"id": "08952206-d196-4c92-861e-3bcc72423ce0", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "tool_summary", "content": [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "tooluse_NwXvwGMojPvuLLCTB68hAH", "status": "success", "content": [{"text": "{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"status\":\"SUCCESS\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/framework/sus_sus_region_a2.html\",\"content\":\"# SUS01-BP01 Choose Region based on both business requirements and sustainability goals\\n\\nChoose a Region for your workload based on both your business requirements\\nand sustainability goals to optimize its KPIs, including performance, cost,\\nand carbon footprint.\\n\\n**Common anti-patterns:**\\n\\n* You select the workload\u2019s Region based on your own location.\\n* You consolidate all workload resources into one geographic location.\\n\\n**Benefits of establishing this best practice:** Placing a workload\\nclose to Amazon renewable energy projects or Regions with low published carbon intensity can help\\nto lower the carbon footprint of a cloud workload.\\n\\n**Level of risk exposed if this best practice\\nis not established:** Medium\\n\\n## Implementation guidance\\n\\nThe AWS Cloud is a constantly expanding network of Regions and points of presence (PoP),\\nwith a global network infrastructure linking them together. The choice of Region for your\\nworkload significantly affects its KPIs, including performance, cost, and carbon footprint.\\nTo effectively improve these KPIs, you should choose Regions for your workload based on\\nboth your business requirements and sustainability goals.\\n\\n### Implementation steps\\n\\n* **Shortlist potential Regions:** Follow these steps to assess and shortlist potential Regions for your workload\\n  based on your business requirements, including compliance, available features,\\n  cost, and latency:\\n\\n  + Confirm that these Regions are compliant, based on your required local regulations (for example, data sovereignty).\\n  + Use the AWS Regional Services Lists to check if the Regions have the services and features you need to run your workload.\\n  + Calculate the cost of the workload on each Region using the AWS Pricing Calculator.\\n  + Test the network latency between your end user locations and each AWS Region.\\n* **Choose Regions:** Choose Regions near Amazon renewable energy projects and Regions where the grid has a\\n  published carbon intensity that is lower than other locations (or Regions).\\n\\n  + Identify your relevant sustainability guidelines to track and compare year-to-year\\n    carbon emissions based on Greenhouse Gas Protocol (market-based and location based methods).\\n  + Choose region based on method you use to track carbon emissions. For more detail\\n    on choosing a Region based on your sustainability guidelines, see\\n    How to select a Region for your workload based on sustainability goals.\\n\\n## Resources\\n\\n**Related documents:**\\n\\n* Understanding your carbon emission estimations\\n* Amazon\\n  Around the Globe\\n* Renewable\\n  Energy Methodology\\n* What\\n  to Consider when Selecting a Region for your Workloads\\n\\n**Related videos:**\\n\\n* AWS re:Invent 2023 - Sustainability innovation in AWS Global Infrastructure\\n* AWS re:Invent 2023 - Sustainable architecture: Past, present, and future\\n* AWS re:Invent 2022 - Delivering sustainable, high-performing architectures\\n* AWS re:Invent 2022 - Architecting sustainably and reducing your AWS carbon footprint\\n* AWS re:Invent 2022 - Sustainability in AWS global infrastructure\",\"total_length\":3044,\"start_index\":0,\"end_index\":3044,\"truncated\":false,\"redirected_url\":null,\"error_code\":null}]}}"}]}], "label": "Fetch AWS Well-Architected Sustainability Pillar Region Selection best practices page"}

Scale infrastructure to continually match demand and verify that you use only the minimum resources required to support your users. Align service levels to customer needs. Position resources to limit the network required for users and applications to consume them. Remove unused assets. Provide your team members with devices that support their needs and minimize their sustainability impact.\\n\\n###### Best practices\\n\\n* SUS02-BP01 Scale workload infrastructure dynamically\\n* SUS02-BP02 Align SLAs with sustainability goals\\n* SUS02-BP03 Stop the creation and maintenance of unused assets\\n* SUS02-BP04 Optimize geographic placement of workloads based on their networking requirements\\n* SUS02-BP05 Optimize team member resources for activities performed\\n* SUS02-BP06 Implement buffering or throttling to flatten the demand curve\",\"total_length\":1021,\"start_index\":0,\"end_index\":1021,\"truncated\":false,\"redirected_url\":null,\"error_code\":null}]}}"}]}], "label": "Fetch AWS docs SUS02 Alignment to demand best practices list"}

Components might become idle from lack of use because of changes in user behavior over time. Revise patterns and architecture to consolidate under-utilized components to increase overall utilization. Retire components that are no longer required. Understand the performance of your workload components, and optimize the components that consume the most resources. Be aware of the devices that your customers use to access your services, and implement patterns to minimize the need for device upgrades.\\n\\n###### Best practices\\n\\n* SUS03-BP01 Optimize software and architecture for asynchronous and scheduled jobs\\n* SUS03-BP02 Remove or refactor workload components with low or no use\\n* SUS03-BP03 Optimize areas of code that consume the most time or resources\\n* SUS03-BP04 Optimize impact on devices and equipment\\n* SUS03-BP05 Use software patterns and architectures that best support data access and storage patterns\",\"total_length\":1176,\"start_index\":0,\"end_index\":1176,\"truncated\":false,\"redirected_url\":null,\"error_code\":null}]}}"}]}], "label": "Fetch AWS docs SUS03 Software and architecture best practices list"}
